transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because I can’t shake this feeling that I’ve messed everything up. I’ve fallen behind at work, and the apartment situation feels like it’s gotten out of control. It’s like I’ve ruined things for everyone, and honestly… I feel like I deserve whatever bad thing happens next.
Have you had thoughts of killing yourself?
I’ve had thoughts like… it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up. I don’t have a plan to hurt myself, but I do catch myself thinking nobody would have to deal with me anymore if I were gone.
Did these feelings start after a particular stressful event?
Yeah. It started after the pipe burst and I had to move into that smaller apartment. My routines kind of fell apart after that. It’s been going on for about a year and two months now.
Before the pipe burst, had you ever gone through another period like this, when you felt depressed or hopeless most days for a while?
I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had bad weeks before, like anyone, but not something that felt like this or lasted most days for a long time before the pipe burst.
During the last two weeks, have you felt down or depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Yeah… most days, pretty much. I wake up with this flat, heavy sadness, and it stays with me a lot of the day. Stuff that used to help, like putting on a record or cooking or messing with electronics, it just doesn’t really reach me anymore.
Because of how you've been feeling, have you been able to keep up with basic daily tasks like getting dressed, showering, and eating regular meals?

I can do the basics, mostly. I’m still getting dressed and eating, though not always on a great schedule. But keeping up with normal routines is harder than it used to be.

I’m still working, but I had to ask for some accommodations and extra review because I’ve been making documentation mistakes I normally wouldn’t. And outside of work, I skip some board-game nights and leave the apartment less. It just feels like more effort than it should.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about many different parts of your life, even when they’re not related to the apartment situation?

I’m not sure I’d say “many different parts.” Most of it circles back to the apartment and what happened there. I get stressed about work sometimes too, but I don’t think I’m worrying about everything across the board.
Do you feel your reaction to the apartment situation has been stronger than most people would have had in the same situation?
I’m not really sure. I mean, it feels strong to me, but I don’t know what most people would do in the same situation. I haven’t really compared it that way.
If the apartment situation were completely resolved tomorrow, do you think you would still feel this depressed?

Yeah… I think I probably would. The apartment thing is a big part of it, but most days I wake up with this flat, heavy sadness anyway. Stuff that used to help me feel normal—putting on a record, cooking something, messing around with electronics—just doesn’t really reach me like it used to.
Have you been waking up much earlier than usual and then unable to get back to sleep?

Yeah. I’ll be up for hours first, just lying there listening for noises from the apartment, and when I finally do fall asleep I wake up before dawn. Then I’m already tense and exhausted, like I never really shut off.
Have you noticed your appetite has decreased?
I haven’t really noticed a big decrease, no. My eating’s maybe a little irregular, but I wouldn’t say my appetite has clearly dropped.
Do you feel worthless, or like you’re a bad person?

Yeah… I do. I keep thinking I’ve messed everything up for everyone—falling behind at work, not handling the apartment situation right. It makes me feel like I’m a bad person, like whatever happens next is probably what I deserve.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah. Most days I wake up with this heavy, flat sadness, and the things I usually enjoy just don’t do much for me anymore. Like putting on a record, cooking, messing with electronics… they used to help me feel more like myself, but lately they don’t really reach me.
